#### §6: Multibyte text, wide characters and conversion

| ID | Spec | Ann. | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-6.1 | §6.1 | HIST | **Internal:** explicit `Decoder`/`Encoder` state values per codec. **Boundary:** `mbstate_t` is an 8-byte serialisation of that state (`legacy::mb_state`), which suffices for all built-in codecs. Its kind, need and have bytes sit in the header's `__count` (offset 0), the value in `__value`; `mbsinit` is true exactly when `__count` is 0, whatever `__value` holds, as the reference answers for a state a program wrote itself (gnulib's replacement converters keep their own partial characters there and ask the C library's `mbsinit`; validation T18, 2026-10-05). A NULL `s` in `mbrtowc`, `mbrtoc32`, `mbrtoc16` and `mbrtoc8` stores nothing through the output pointer (C17 7.29.6.3.2, 7.28.1: the call is `mbrtowc(NULL, "", 1, ps)`; the reference agrees). |
| D-6.2 | §6.2 | HIST, PATH | **Internal:** results are `Decoded::{Char(u32, len), Null, Incomplete, Invalid, SurrogateContinuation}`. **Boundary:** `(size_t)-1/-2/-3` via `abi::ret`. The non-restartable forms use a per-thread state (P-scope). |
| D-6.3 | §6.3 | HIST | **Internal:** conversion into a caller slice returns `Converted{written, consumed, needed}`, or allocates an owned result. **Boundary:** the NULL-destination measuring mode is one conversion choice (`conv::opt_buf`). |
| D-6.4 | §6.4 | HIST | **Internal:** iconv is built in (no gconv module loading; F28). `IGNORE`/`TRANSLIT` report counts of dropped and approximated characters separately. **Boundary:** reproduces "-1/EILSEQ at end if anything was ignored", per the contract. |
| D-6.5 | §6.2 | HIST, ARB | `MB_CUR_MAX` is 6 for UTF-8 locales, per the contract, because programs size buffers from it. Internally, UTF-8 needs at most 4. |
| D-6.6 | §6.5 | HIST | **Internal:** `display_width(u32, AmbiguousWidth::{Narrow, Wide})`. **Boundary:** narrow is the default. |
| D-6.7 | §5–§7 | ARB (spec silent) | **Approved.** The built-in `"C"`/`"POSIX"` locale's charset is ASCII. Bytes 0x80–0xFF: no class, mapped to themselves by `tolower`/`toupper`, `mbrtowc` fails with `EILSEQ`, `btowc` returns `WEOF`, `wctob` of a code point above 0x7F returns `EOF`, and `MB_CUR_MAX` is 1. | D-6.8 | §6.2–6.4 | HIST | **Charsets from the system charmaps** (owner ruling 2026-10-01, phase 7; refines D-6.4). Built in, with no file access: UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32, UCS-2 and UCS-4 (both byte orders and the BOM forms), `WCHAR_T`, ASCII (`ANSI_X3.4-1968`) and ISO-8859-1. Every other charset is read on first use from `/usr/share/i18n/charmaps/<name>.gz` (or uncompressed): installed system data in the POSIX charmap format, read under the format-inspection decision. Its `<code_set_name>`, `% alias` lines, `<mb_cur_max>` and mapping lines (including `<U…>..<U…>` ranges) are compiled in memory into a decoding trie and an encoding map, cached per process and immutable. Gzip decompression (RFC 1951/1952) is a small safe-Rust inflater in core. Stateful encodings that glibc implements only in modules (ISO-2022 family, UTF-7, stateful EBCDIC) are not supported: `iconv_open` reports `EINVAL` (deviation). A locale whose codeset has no codec (charmaps not installed) fails to load its `LC_CTYPE`. Charset names match case-insensitively, through the charmap's name and aliases. **Compared with the reference iconv** (all 231 charmaps that list mappings, every mapping of small charsets and an even sample of large ones, both directions): 200 agree exactly; 26 are unknown to the reference iconv; 5 differ where the charmap and glibc's module disagree, and Liella follows the charmap: the teletex sets (ANSI_X3.110-1983, ISO-IR-90, ISO_6937, T.61-8BIT) list their non-spacing diacritic prefixes as private-use code points that the modules combine with the next letter, and MAC-CYRILLIC's 0xA2 is U+00A2 in the charmap, U+0490 in the module. Composing charsets (TCVN5712-1, TSCII) decode the longest listed sequence; a code point listed under several sequences encodes as the lowest. **Names** match a charmap's name and aliases as codeset names do (case and punctuation aside: `eucjp` is `EUC-JP`). A name no loaded charmap answers to is tried as a file name, then found by a scan of the directory: first by file name, then by the header's `<code_set_name>` and aliases (read from the first 4 KiB of each file, without parsing it). Runs of mappings that continue one another merge into one range when parsed, so the 8-bit charsets search a few ranges. **Locale differential test** (`locale_products`, adds ja_JP.EUC-JP, ru_RU.KOI8-R and zh_CN.GB18030): `mbrtowc` returns −2 only for a valid prefix (§6.2), where the reference also returns it for a prefix no character extends (UTF-8 `ED A0`, a surrogate; EUC-JP's lone 0xA0); and the GB18030 charmap lists supplementary characters only up to its Unicode version (U+1F600 is absent), where the reference module maps the whole linear four-byte range. The test records these three lines and fails if one stops differing. **Owner: the recorded differences are accepted (2026-10-01).** GB18030's newer characters stay as the charmap gives them; revisit only if they cause coreutils failures (phase 15). (Amended by D-6.15, D-6.16, D-6.17.) |
| D-6.9 | §6.4 | HIST, ARB | **iconv** (phase 7; refines D-6.4). A descriptor decodes to code points and encodes from them (pivot UCS-4), with its decoder and encoder states in the descriptor, so a conversion resumes at any split point. `//TRANSLIT` uses the current `LC_CTYPE` locale's transliteration table (Appendix D.1.3) and its default replacement. The built-in `C`, `POSIX` and `C.UTF-8` locales have no table file; their transliteration is derived from the UCD and is not the reference library's table, which the spec does not give: in `C.UTF-8`, a character's full decomposition without combining marks; in `C` and `POSIX`, only a decomposition that involves a compatibility mapping, with marks kept (they then become `?`, as in the reference `C` locale); then an ASCII-equivalents table (quotes, dashes, guillemets, `© ® ™ € × ⁄`, `ß æ œ` and their capitals); a vulgar fraction is set off by spaces (` 1/2 `); what still does not convert becomes `?`. `//IGNORE` reports as the contract says (−1/`EILSEQ` at the end if anything was dropped). **The reference library's behaviour, observed and followed** (phase 7; compared line by line by `iconv_products.rs`): `UTF-16` and `UTF-32` read an optional BOM in either order and otherwise assume little-endian; written, they begin with a little-endian BOM, once per descriptor until a reset or flush (no room for it is `E2BIG`); the forms that name an order neither read nor write one. `UCS-2` is little-endian, `UCS-4` big-endian, `WCHAR_T` little-endian. Every UTF-16 and UCS-2 form rejects surrogates. The `UCS-4` forms carry values up to `0x7FFFFFFF`, which `UTF-8` writes in the original 5- and 6-byte forms; `UTF-16`, `UTF-32` and the byte charsets reject values above U+10FFFF. Suffixes count on the target name only, separated by `/` or `,`, in any case; unknown ones are ignored. Incomplete input stays in the caller's buffer (`EINVAL`). With `//IGNORE`, invalid input is skipped as well; `E2BIG` still reports first, and an incomplete end after a drop is `EILSEQ`. The empty name is the current `LC_CTYPE` codeset. **Recorded differences** (the test lists them and fails if one stops differing): ISO-2022-JP and UTF-7 (stateful, D-6.8); the alias `WINDOWS-1252`, which no charmap lists; CP932's U+2014, which WINDOWS-31J's charmap does not map. **Owner: accepted (2026-10-01).** |
| D-6.10 | §6.2 | PERF | **The single-character decoders read their input lazily (AUD-M4).** `mbrtowc`, `mbrtoc32/16/8`, `mbrlen`, `mbtowc`, `mblen` read the text one byte at a time (`strz::LazyText`, `mb_compat::MbInput`) and stop where the character does: no `strnlen` over `n` (a loop `mbrtowc(p, end - p)` was O(N^2)), and no byte past the character is touched (the reference returns 1 for an `A` ending a page before an inaccessible one with `n` 100000; Liella faulted: probe 551e4d076fae). Residual difference: in a multibyte charmap locale a complete character at a page end before an unreadable page may still read one byte more than the reference. Tests: `single_character_forms_read_no_byte_past_the_character` (boundary, guard page), `single_character_forms_read_only_the_character` (core, counts bytes read). MB-K2: UTF-8 from the initial state is read and decoded in one pass (`text::decode_utf8_initial`, same rules, bytes read, answer and state as the per-byte loop; `mbrtoc16`/`mbrtoc8` apply `split_utf16`/`split_utf8_units` to its result); `utf8_fast_path_matches_the_per_byte_definition` also compares the state left. WL-HOT-SEQ3: `mbrtowc`/`__mbrtowc`/`mbrtoc32`/`mbrlen`/`__mbrlen` answer at the export, before the lazy reader and the state machinery, when `s` is non-NULL, `n >= 1` and the state (caller's or hidden) is all zero bytes: a byte below 0x80 in a UTF-8 or ASCII locale, or a well-formed two-byte UTF-8 character with `n >= 2`; the state is left as is (the general path stores the same zero bytes). Test: `single_character_quick_path_matches_the_general_decoder` (every 1-2 byte input, n 0..3, against a zero-__count non-zero state that takes the general path). WL-HOT-SEQ4: the 2-byte en_US.UTF-8 'regression' (wl_percall 237 -> 260) was the probe, not the library: its spec never called setlocale, so it ran in the C locale (encoding Ascii: the ASCII quick path applies, a 0xC3 lead correctly declines). | D-6.17 | §6.4 | HIST | **How `iconv_open` matches a charset name** (ICONV-NAME-MATCH, GitHub issue #6; amends D-6.8). The text before the suffixes is reduced to a matching form, then compared exactly with the known names: the built-in table and each installed charmap's name and aliases, reduced the same way. Letters are uppercased. Letters, digits and `, - . / : _` count. Every other byte (space, control, other ASCII punctuation, any byte above 0x7F) is dropped. The name is `PART[/PART2]`, and the suffixes start after the second `/`. Trailing commas of the second part are dropped. When the second part is then empty, the name is the first part without its trailing commas. A name longer than 128 bytes in matching form names nothing. So `iso88591` opens (`ISO88591` is a known name of ISO-8859-1), `iso 8859 1//TRANSLIT` opens with transliteration, and `cp-1252` names nothing (the `-` counts). Conversions match charmaps this way; locale codesets keep their own normalisation (letters and digits only, Appendix D.1). The rule and its evidence (a black-box probe table of 32,915 spellings over the 1,180 names of `iconv -l`) are in `spec/encoding/iconv-names.md`. It replaces the earlier matching: built-ins compared ignoring case only, charmaps compared by letters and digits alone. That accepted `cp-1252` and rejected ` utf-8`. The known names also include a table of 106 names that `iconv -l` lists on the reference system and that stand for a charmap under another spelling (`KOI8R` for `KOI8-R`, `ISO885915` for `ISO-8859-15`; `crates/core/src/iconv/aliases.rs`). The earlier loose match had found these names in any installed charmap set. They are consulted only after the loaded charmaps, so an open of a charmap already in memory costs nothing extra. Each row passed a black-box check on the reference: both names convert every one- and two-byte input and every code point alike. Listing (`iconv -l`) is unchanged apart from the added built-in name `ISO88591`. (Amended by D-6.20.) |

CP949 (Unified Hangul Code) is a sixth set of D-6.18's generic codec: its table is the Unicode Consortium's `VENDORS/MICSFT/WINDOWS/CP949.TXT` (table version 2.01, 1/7/2000), vendored unchanged; the reference's variant (`spec/encoding/reference/CP949.tsv`) holds no cell or encoding departure from that table, only the leads, the trails, the bytes skipped alone and that a skipping `//IGNORE` call ends with `EILSEQ`. Read-only data by generator output: CP949 108,801 bytes. Names, each probed on the reference to be one converter (whole dump hashed): CP949, UHC, MSCP949, OSF100203B5, any case (`CP-949`, `MS949`, `WINDOWS-949`, `KS_C_5601-1987`, `KSC5601` do not open there and stay out). The pair A2E8, which CP949.TXT does not assign, is an invalid sequence with nothing consumed and is skipped whole with `//IGNORE` (unit test `cp949_cells_and_unassigned_pair`). The table of listed names that stand for a charmap (D-6.17's table, 104 rows on next, by the same-letters-and-digits rule) is now data, `spec/encoding/iconv-aliases.tsv` (654 rows, the 104 earlier rows among them unchanged), and `csys/util/iconv-aliases.h` for the command, both written by `tools/probe/iconv_aliases.py` from a black-box probe of the reference: every name its `iconv -l` lists that is neither a built-in name nor a charmap file name gets a row naming the charmap whose reference conversion has the same fingerprint (`tools/probe/iconv_fingerprint.c`: every one- and two-byte input decoded, every BMP code point and a stride of the rest encoded). A charmap's conversion is taken through its file name and the names its installed file gives, not through the aliases libniji's generated charmaps add (CP9448, which CP1256's generated charmap carries, converts otherwise on the reference and has no row). `WINDOWS-1252` and `windows-1251` failed because only the generated charmaps carried them; they are rows now. The library reads the rows at compile time as byte offsets into the file's bytes (no relocation, no start-up page). 220 listed names have no conversion in libniji (EBCDIC and double-byte IBM sets with no installed charmap, `ISO-2022-*`, `UTF-7`, ...) and no row; names with a `/` are left out. Nineteen listed names that convert as a built-in (`ANSI_X3.4`, `CSWINDOWS31J`, `UNICODE`, ...) became built-in names. `iconv -l` also lists each row whose charmap is an installed file, or opens under another file's name (CP874 in IBM874's header; that charmap name is listed too, each such charmap tried once): on the reference system (Ubuntu 24.04 charmaps) libniji lists 982 of the reference's 1,180 names plus 26 charmap file names the reference does not list. |
